question_text: In designing the hull of a new fishing vessel to ensure corrosion protection, you find that a sacrificial anode of zinc provides an average corrosion current of 2 A over the period of 1 year. What mass of zinc is required to give this protection?The unit of the answer is kg.
response:
Using Faraday's law of electrolysis, $m = \frac{M I t}{n F}$:

- $M_{\text{Zn}} = 65.38\ \text{g/mol}$, $n = 2$ (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻), $F = 96485\ \text{C/mol}$
- $I = 2\ \text{A}$, $t = 1\ \text{yr} = 365\times24\times3600 = 3.1536\times10^{7}\ \text{s}$
- Total charge $Q = It = 6.3072\times10^{7}\ \text{C}$
- $m = \frac{65.38 \times 6.3072\times10^{7}}{2 \times 96485} \approx 21369\ \text{g} \approx 21.37\ \text{kg}$

$$\boxed{21.37}$$
